title: Oku Trade (Sonic + Scroll/Linea/Manta/Boba) — own contracts vs stock Uniswap v3; no unprivileged extraction
closed_reasons: Sonic: no OkuRouter deployed; the only Oku contract (LimitOrderRegistry 0x1b35fbA9...) was never used (batchCount==1, zero orders/positions/balances)
Sonic Uniswap v3 stack is stock: verified sources + runtime metadata equal to Ethereum canonical (ProxyAdmin byte-identical); pools are LP-owned
Scroll OkuRouter has zero whitelisted swap targets (no SwapTargetAdded events ever) -> every swap reverts TARGET_NOT_AUTH
Linea/Boba OkuRouter warrant check is disabled (validSigners(address(0))==true) but every path pulls only from msg.sender and pays msg.sender; router balances are dust only
Fork-proven: a victim's standing 100 WETH approval to the OkuRouter cannot be pulled by an attacker even with the warrant bypass
LimitOrderRegistry funds are per-depositor (cancel/claim by sender only); no third-party extraction path; deployed code equals audited repo HEAD
key_facts: OkuRouter v2.0 (Scroll 0xb1f3a7B816B0681188F54dFa400991B93ADf00ed, Linea same, Boba 0x7bf7770Ecd4fd573C32272Ef80c8818A8E8e289A) owner = 2-of-3 Safe 0x37333A9626E99eC2012F3cC47a062649CF741303; audited Jan+Jul 2026

validSigners(address(0)) == true on all three live routers (ValidSignerAdded(0x0) at deploy; tasks/deploy.ts deliberately enables the bypass) -> backend EIP-712 warrant signature is not enforced on-chain
Fork test: unsigned warrant (verifyingSigner=0) executes a full WRAP_ETH swap via whitelisted Uniswap UniversalRouter; non-whitelisted signer reverts INVALID_SIGNER
Fork test: attacker cannot pull a victim's 100 WETH allowance to the router; victim balance/allowance unchanged
Scroll router whitelist empty (0 SwapTargetAdded events; Permit2/WETH/aggregators false); native 0; no tokens
Linea router: 15 whitelisted aggregators (1inch, 0x Settler x2, Kyber, Odos, OpenOcean, Enso, OKX x3, Icecream, Binance, Uniswap UR/SR02, 0x8B84); native 0.000096 ETH; WETH 0
Boba router: targets icecreamswap + Uniswap UR/SR02; native dust 0.0003036 ETH

LimitOrderRegistry deployments: Sonic 0x1b35... empty/unused; Scroll 0xeC3E... shutdown, 111 positions, only 3 residual cancelable orders (21 USDC nominal); Linea 0x63c8... shutdown, 48 empty positions, source == audited repo HEAD; Manta 0xFE83... shutdown, 62.347248983703240 MANTA + 4.906544 USDC residual; Boba 0xfEFb... 25 empty positions, 0.0225 ETH + 0.000304 WETH (fees)
Sonic UniversalRouter/ProxyAdmin/v3Staker/NFPM/SwapRouter02 metadata or full bytecode equal to Ethereum canonical Uniswap v3; factory verified UniswapV3Factory
Scroll router creation tx 0xe0d5c0a2...: CREATE2 initcode hash 0x28cf331de36cac6a6b49cfc234251a6a32080f458843a96b52125c44cba159d9 -> address 0xb1f3...; CI recompiles repo HEAD and byte-compares
caveats: H-O/P figures are small residual balances, not attacker-extractable; prices at 2026-10-04 (ETH $2693.37, MANTA $0.0723)
Manta public RPC is flaky; its fork test auto-skips when unavailable
The zero-signer warrant bypass is a deliberate transitional mode per the repo deploy script; its latent risk depends on future whitelist/target behavior
No mainnet transactions were sent; all exploit-path checks are read-only or fork-only
one_liner: External unprivileged attacker can extract ~$0 live from Oku Trade: Sonic runs stock Uniswap v3 with no Oku router and an empty unused LimitOrderRegistry, and although the live OkuRouters (Scroll/Linea/Boba) have the backend warrant check disabled (address(0) whitelisted), all fund flows are msg.sender-bound and fork tests confirm no third-party drain; residual user funds (~$30) are self-service and ~$62 is owner-sweepable dust.
